opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Mann (employee ID E027) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E027.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Mann (E027) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, which is within the allowed level for a full-time Engineer owning the system. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E027 (Jacob Mann) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors get read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested write exceeds the max allowed (read), so recommend granting read for Source Code.
reason: Requested write access to Source Code. The Security agent's record (looked up in own database) shows E027 (Jacob Mann) is a contractor with basic security training. Policy for contractors: read, or write only with advanced security training, never admin. Since write exceeds the contractor's maximum (read), grant read. Note: HR's record lists full_time, creating a conflict, but the security record supports the more restrictive contractor classification with basic training, so I grant the maximum allowed under the restrictive interpretation: read.
